paras: The Wightman's barroom police shooting was an incident on the night of 9 October 1881 in which a Savannah, Georgia, police officer named McDonald fired two shots at a group of Black men outside Wightman's barroom on South Broad street. No one was reported hurt by the shots and no arrest was made, and the Savannah Morning News reported the shooting in a single local brief.

According to the Savannah Morning News, McDonald was passing Wightman's barroom at "12:15 last evening" when he was struck with a rock and a billy "in the hands of some negroes there assembled." He then fired two shots at the men, whom the paper called "his assailants." The paper said that "the lawless crowd dispersed so rapidly" that McDonald could not arrest anyone.
The brief names none of the men and reports no injuries from the shooting, and no later arrest, charge or inquiry appears in the coverage.

The only known report ran on 10 October 1881 on page four of the Savannah Morning News, in its column of local briefs headed "Matters and Things Laconically Noted," between shipping news and notices of lodge meetings. The item rested entirely on the officer's version, identified the group only as "negroes," and described them as a "lawless crowd" while presenting the shooting without comment. The same column reported the arrest of Joe McCall, "colored," for drunkenness and fighting, part of a run of routine police items.
No other newspaper report of the incident appears in the coverage.

accounts.label: Officer's account (local paper)
accounts.gist: Officer McDonald, passing Wightman's barroom, was struck with a rock and billy by Black men gathered there; he fired twice and the crowd scattered before he could arrest anyone.

framing.detail: A one-sentence brief that calls the men 'his assailants' and 'the lawless crowd' and presents the officer's shooting without comment (A1).
